Subject: Findly / Redwood — Reranker integration follow-ups & evaluation Qs

Hi Rachel — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we’re aligned on scope for the POC and the evaluation phase.

High-level goals (what Findly asked for):
- Improve precision on top-ranked results for enterprise docs search (reduce noise in top 10).
- Keep end-to-end query latency under ~150ms median for UIs with caching.
- Verify reranker gives clear uplift vs current BM25+embedding baseline on business slices.

Architecture / integration items we discussed:
- Candidate generation: you’ll run your current ES + embedding similarity to produce ~100 candidates per query (K_gen=100).
- Reranker: Redwood will score and reorder candidates; recommended top_k_rerank = 10 for UI.
- SDK & auth: POC can use API key from Redwood SDK; we recommend mTLS or customer-managed KMS for production.
- Routing/fallbacks: plan routing policy where cheaper model variant is used for non-critical endpoints; fallback to embeddings-only when GPU capacity constrained.
- Structured output/tool-calls: not required for initial POC; later roadmap item if you want answer synthesis or cite links.

Evaluation questions we need Findly to answer / provide:
1) Sample queries + labels: a CSV with ~1k queries and binary relevance labels (or graded 0-2).
2) Priority slices: identify business-critical query subsets (e.g., contracts, invoices, onboarding docs).
3) Latency SLOs & throughput: expected QPS and per-request latency targets.
4) Cost constraints: rough monthly query volume for cost tradeoffs.

Attachments: findly-sample-queries.csv (placeholder for your sample).

Next steps / owners: 
- Rachel: share labeled sample and a drive link (by Fri 11/6).
- Vanessa: send a short evaluation rubric and metric suggestions (tomorrow).
- Rishi: scope Dedicated vs Hosted capacity options once we see throughput numbers.
- Karthik (me): put together mutual action plan & timeline after we get dataset.

Thanks — Karthik

Hi Rachel — quick technical notes / recommendations based on the questions above. Attaching a short guidance doc (eval-metrics-guidance.md).

Evaluation metrics (recommended):
- Primary: NDCG@10 (captures graded relevance and position sensitivity).
- Secondary: MRR for single-click scenarios and Recall@100 to measure candidate generation coverage.
- Report: show NDCG@1, @3, @10 and delta vs your current baseline. Provide per-slice breakdown (contracts / onboarding / help center).

Candidate generation size:
- 200 is fine for the POC (K_gen=200). We typically prune duplicates and near-duplicates before rerank to avoid wasted tokens.

Top_k tuning guidance:
- Candidate gen K_gen = 200, rerank top_k_rerank = 10 (UI) or 20 (batch scoring).
- Evaluate NDCG curves for top_k_rerank in {5,10,20} to find diminishing returns point.

Latency & batching:
- For interactive UI target ~150ms median, recommend micro-batching window <= 20ms and a tail SLO of 300ms.
- If you use embeddings-only fallback during spikes, seen 2–3x cost reduction while preserving availability.

Auth & SDK:
- POC: API key via Redwood SDK (fast).
- Production: mTLS or OAuth + customer KMS for keys; we support both. Also can whitelist by VPC for Private deployments.

Structured output / tool calling:
- If you plan to show synthesized answers with citations, we should design a post-rerank synthesis step that takes the top 5 documents and emits structured citations. Keep that for a second phase.

Attachment: eval-metrics-guidance.md (short checklist).

—Vanessa
